analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/architecture/prefix-cache.md. Head lines 295 and 300-306 add the plain unpublished Nemotron Super owner to the opt-in resident recurrent checkpoint bank gate. They also add chunk-aligned recurrent capture (alignsRecurrentCheckpointsToPrefillChunks, NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache). No code, endpoint or deployment change is visible in the supplied patch or surrounding doc.

Relevant threats: T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and TTFT oracle). The doc keeps the existing statements that the resident bank requires DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1, is tenant-scoped by cacheSalt, writes nothing to disk, and uses the slot KV grant. The doc also keeps the global DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 kill switch (lines 287-288). The new model is described as adopting through the same bank and the same cacheSalt scoping, so no new at-rest surface or tenant-isolation claim is introduced by the text.

Coverage limits: the actual Nemotron Super implementation (NemotronSuperLocalPrefixCache, its capture and eligibility gates, and the claimed bit-exact restore) is not in the supplied evidence. I could not verify the text against code, and the claim of continuing a cold chunk partition bit for bit is unverified. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the range map is marked complete. A later pass that sees the code should confirm cacheSalt scoping, the memory opt-in gate, and the model-identity binding for the new owner. T-041 may need a note if Nemotron Super becomes reachable through the resident bank by default. No findings.
